I am 36, been farming my 9.2 mu since I was 16. Never went to school. My father taught me, and I watch what the neighbors do. If it works on their field, it works on mine. Last year my wheat made about 550 jin per mu and my maize made 650 jin. I will do the same as last year because change is risky and a bad harvest means my family goes hungry.

For the winter wheat: I use improved seed from the village dealer, the kind everyone buys. I sow it in October. Before sowing, I hire the tractor to rotary till the field. I spread one 50-jin bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer on each mu. When the wheat turns green and gets up in spring, I topdress with 25 jin of urea per mu. I water four times: the overwinter water, the jointing water, the heading water, and the grain filling water. I spray twice: once for weeds in early spring, and once for rust and aphids before the heads come out.

For the summer maize: As soon as the wheat is harvested in June, I plant hybrid maize seed, the kind with the big ears that my neighbor Lao Wang used. I plant 2.5 jin per mu. There is no time to plough — I plant no-till straight into the wheat stubble. At planting I put down 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. When the plants are knee-high, I spread 20 jin of urea per mu. I water three times: at planting if the ground is dry, at the big trumpet stage, and at filling. I spray twice: once for weeds after the seedlings are up, and once for corn borer when I see the moths flying around.

I know fertilizer is expensive this year. Urea is over 100 yuan per bag, compound is nearly 180. But I will not cut back. Wasting some fertilizer is just money down the drain. Losing yield is a disaster. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends money home, so I can pay for the inputs. I have 9.2 mu — not the smallest farm, not the biggest. I mostly work it myself and with my brother, but I hire help at harvest if we are short on time. If I am not sure about something, I do what I did before. That has kept my family fed for 20 years.
